Operation: Doomsday is the debut solo studio album by British-American rapper MF Doom, originally released on October 19, 1999, through the independent label Fondle 'Em Records. This album marked MF Doom's reinvention after his earlier career as Zev Love X in the group KMD and personal tragedies, establishing his supervillain persona inspired by the comic character Doctor Doom. Musically, the album features a lo-fi, underground hip-hop style characterized by dusty, sample-heavy beats, cartoon and comic book references, and MF Doom’s distinctive, intricate rhyme schemes delivered in a laid-back, sometimes slurred flow. The production and lyrical content blend elements of 1980s soul, classic hip-hop, and surreal storytelling, creating a unique, unorthodox sound that stands apart from mainstream rap of the time.

Within MF Doom’s discography, Operation: Doomsday is seminal as his first solo statement and is widely regarded as a cult classic and one of the most influential independent hip-hop albums ever released. It set the tone for his career, showcasing his creativity and lyrical prowess while embracing underground aesthetics. The album includes notable tracks like “Doomsday,” which remains one of his most popular songs, exemplifying his clever wordplay and thematic depth.
